report.verdict: A decent operating quarter wrapped around a bad guidance quarter. UK online grew 12.2% cc to a third straight record NGR with less marketing, Q3 AEBITDA rose 5.1% QoQ to €88.9m (~$97.5m) and the margin recovered 50bps to 31.1% — but management cut FY26 AEBITDA guidance for the second time in three months to €380–395m (~$417–433m) from €402–415m (and ~€422m originally), because the 40% UK remote gaming duty is still only ~55% offset, UK consolidation is "slower than I expected" and US lottery is soft. Pro forma leverage drifted to 4.33x into the January 2027 evoke close, and the implied Q4 (€106–121m vs €88.9m in Q3) looks stretched.

summary: **Headline: operations fine, guidance not.** 9M26 revenue €830.3m (~$911m) and AEBITDA €273.6m (~$300m, 33.0% margin) — not comparable with 9M25 (€263.9m / €90.1m) because Bally's International Interactive (BII) was consolidated from 8 Oct 2025. On the company's own pro forma comparable, 9M AEBITDA fell 14.7% from €320.8m. Q3 revenue €286.1m (~$314m), +3.6% QoQ; AEBITDA €88.9m (~$97.5m), +5.1% QoQ; margin 31.1%, +50bps QoQ but −540bps YoY (3Q25: 36.5%).

**Second guidance cut in three months.** FY26 AEBITDA now €380–395m (~$417–433m): BII €270–280m (~$296–307m) and legacy Intralot €110–115m (~$121–126m). August: €402–415m (BII €280–295m, legacy €112–120m). March plan, reaffirmed in May: ~€422m (BII c.€299m, legacy c.€124m). Midpoint −€21m (−5%) vs August, −€35m (−8%) vs the original plan. Both ranges now explicitly embed GBP, USD and TRY translation.

**Which division drove it: ~70% BII.** CEO Robeson Reeves put the BII gap at ~€15m — "I got the pace of consolidation wrong, because I expected subscale operators to fall away much faster" — plus a deliberate choice not to strip cost so the team can "hit the ground running" at evoke close. The legacy gap is €5–7.5m "depending on jackpots" (US lottery). Edison (company-sponsored) sits at €387.5m, the midpoint.

**The UK duty is the whole P&L story.** Remote gaming duty rose from 21% to 40% on 1 Apr 2026. Gross AEBITDA hit ~€34m (~$37m) in Q3 (in line with Q2), ~€68m (~$75m) in 9M. 9M offset 48.5% (+€26.2m organic gross-profit growth, +€6.8m fixed-cost actions). Q3 offset ~55% measured YoY — which arithmetically implies ~42% in Q2 on the same basis; the ~65% cited at H1 was measured against the pre-duty run-rate, so the metric's basis has changed. Ex-duty, BII AEBITDA would be +14.4% YoY.

**UK top line is genuinely strong.** UK online revenue +12.2% cc YoY in Q3 (Q1 +10.5%, Q2 +11.6%) — three consecutive accelerations and a third straight record NGR quarter, delivered with marketing lower both YoY and QoQ. 9M UK online +11.4%. Spain hit a record €13.3m (~$14.6m), +18.9% YoY on a larger active base. No actives, ARPU, product split or market-share data are disclosed.

**BII economics.** Q3 revenue €201.6m (~$221m), +4.0% QoQ; 9M €579.2m (~$635m), +10.9% cc pro forma; AEBITDA €62.8m (~$69m) at 31.1% (Q2 31.0%, pre-duty Q1 39.5%); 9M €195.6m (~$215m) at 33.8% — we derive −15.2% vs a €230.7m pro forma 9M25 base. BII is 70% of group revenue and 71% of AEBITDA.

**Legacy Intralot is drifting.** 9M revenue €251.1m (~$276m), −4.9% reported / −3.4% cc; AEBITDA €78.1m (~$86m), −13.4% / −11.9% cc; margin 31.1% vs 34.2%. Legacy B2B AEBITDA €58.4m (~$64m), −15.6% cc, margin 30.6% vs 34.1%, on US revenue −11.0% cc to €119.6m (~$131m) (record 2025 jackpots, lower equipment sales); rest of B2B +3.6% cc. Q3 group B2B AEBITDA €20.2m fell €4.3m QoQ (margin 32.0% vs 37.6%) — not explained in the release.

**Legacy B2C is the bright spot, in lira.** Bilyoner wagers +28.4% LC vs a Turkish online sports-betting market up 17.8% (share gains); revenue +20.6% LC but only +3.4% in EUR to €45.8m (~$50m) on an 18.2% average lira depreciation; Q3 revenue +25.8% QoQ and AEBITDA +€4.7m QoQ after a Q2 hit from seasonality and a remuneration-structure amendment. Argentina +21.1% to €14.3m (~$15.7m). Legacy B2C AEBITDA €19.7m (~$21.6m), +1.8%.

**Below the line, losses are structural for now.** 9M EBT −€21.4m (~−$23m) vs +€8.8m; NIATMI −€40.9m (~−$45m) vs −€3.1m, on net finance costs of €109.7m (~$120m; 9M25 €20.5m), D&A €130.7m (incl. €38.2m PPA) and transaction fees €27.7m (~$30m). Q3 NIATMI −€26.6m (~−$29m). Pro forma LTM PAT is €74.2m vs a reported LTM loss we derive at ~€98.6m. Derived GAAP EPS ~−€0.022 (~−$0.024) on ~1.87bn shares (share capital €560.3m / €0.30 nominal) — not company-reported; no adjusted EPS disclosed.

**Cash flow fine, net debt still creeping up.** 9M OCF €206.6m (~$227m; Q3 €73.2m); net capex €133.3m (~$146m) incl. the €85.0m (~$93m) Victoria 15-year monitoring-licence premium; company-defined FCF €142.9m (~$157m) excludes that premium; FCF to equity €54.5m (~$60m) after €88.4m net interest. Adjusted net debt €1,629.9m (~$1.79bn), +€136.0m YTD (licence €85.0m, deal fees/bond costs €19.5m, other investing €4.0m, non-cash €26.5m), flat QoQ vs €1,618.9m. PF leverage 4.33x vs 4.05x at Q2 as the duty annualises; PF LTM AEBITDA has slid €431m (Dec-25) → €427m (Mar-26) → €399.9m (Jun-26) → €376.7m (Sep-26).

**Liquidity rebuilt with new sterling debt.** £261.8m (~€306m / ~$336m) three-year senior secured term facility signed in July; Tranche A £157.1m (€183.2m / ~$201m) drawn, €65m RCF repaid in August. Liquidity €472.4m (~$518m) = €312.4m cash incl. restricted + undrawn €160m RCF (Jun-26: €287.3m). Funded debt €1,882m: €130m 6.00% retail bond 2029, €600m 6.75% SSNs 2031, €300m FRNs 2031, £400m 2025 term loan (€466.7m), £157.1m 2026 term loan, €200m Greek bank facility.

**Capital returns while 4.3x levered.** €30.0m (~$33m) dividend paid plus €25.5m (~$28m) of buyback/TRS-collateral outflows in 9M — i.e. €55.5m returned against €54.5m of FCFE — and a €43.3m (~$47.5m) total-return-swap liability (Deutsche Bank acquiring shares on the company's behalf) sits outside the "Total Debt" definition. Funding shareholder returns with new debt into a leveraging acquisition is a governance point for both bondholders and minorities.

**evoke on track for January 2027.** All-share acquisition announced 5 June (equity value c.£243m / ~€284m / ~$312m per iGB; EV c.€1.6bn per Edison at the indicated 50p). evoke shareholders approved with 99.63% (18 Aug), BYLOT EGM 18 Sep; UK gaming-regulatory and UK merger-control conditions satisfied; remaining gaming approvals and the Gibraltar court sanction expected by end-2026. The 10 Nov preliminary release said "by Q1-27"; the 20 Nov final firmed this to a January close. No synergy number yet — only "significant cost synergies and growth opportunities". Until close, the two are run as separate competitors.

**Lottery contract renewals bought duration, at a cost.** 2026 wins/renewals: Victoria 15-year EGM monitoring licence (Apr), BCLC shared services (Apr), Polla Chilena (Apr), Hellenic Lotteries (May), OLG Ontario lottery technology (Jun), PLI Ireland to 2034 (Jul); US new-contract go-lives in Montana and Idaho, with Arkansas and New Hampshire in 1H-27. Normalised items show the price of staying in the game: Maryland litigation/RFP costs, the completed Texas RFP (outcome not disclosed), New York and South Carolina RFP preparation, a Croatia software-delay penalty, an ODIE receivable impairment and a Turkish KYC fine.

**Mix has flipped to online.** 9M26 revenue: iGaming & sports betting 75.0% (19.8% in 9M25), lottery 20.3% (68.2%), VLT monitoring 4.0%, casino/other 0.7%; B2C 76.9% / B2B 23.1%. Regionally (chart-derived) UK €540.6m (65%), America ~€150.7m (18%, −9% YoY), Europe €70.7m (9%), RoW €68.3m (8%).

**Cost lines.** Gaming tax €192.2m (~$211m) in 9M, 23.1% of revenue (€76.8m / 26.8% in Q3, ~38% of BII revenue vs ~22% pre-duty); marketing €70.7m (~$78m), 8.5% of revenue (Q3 €21.7m / 7.6%, below the ~€24.5m/qtr 1H run-rate); personnel €130.5m (15.7%; Q3 €42.7m / 14.9%). AEBITDA excludes €21.4m of non-recurring items in 9M (€5.4m in Q3).

**Implied Q4 arithmetic looks stretched (our estimate).** Guidance implies Q4 AEBITDA of €106–121m (~$117–133m) vs €88.9m in Q3 and vs a pro forma Q4-25 of ~€103m (derived: PF LTM €376.7m less 9M26) — flat-to-up YoY despite ~€34m of incremental duty in Q4. BII alone needs €74–84m vs €62.8m in Q3 (+19–34% QoQ), i.e. a >100% YoY duty offset after 55% in Q3. Q4 is seasonally the strongest UK quarter and marketing is already pared, but we regard the bottom of the range as the realistic target with risk below it.

**Management/strategy.** CEO Robeson Reeves (also Bally's Corp CEO), CFO Andreas Chrysos, COO & President Chrysostomos Sfatos, CFO Interactive Katherine Gomaniouk presented. Priorities stated on the call: revenue growth over further marketing cuts; retain cost base for evoke integration; Q2 "was the low point". Bally's Corp consolidates the company and reported its Q3 (Bally's Intralot B2C revenue +22% YoY in USD) on 9/16 Nov.

**Thesis read-through.** BII has shown it can grow through a 40% duty but cannot yet defend EBITDA; the equity case has migrated almost entirely to UK consolidation plus the evoke cost-synergy story, carried on 4.3x leverage pre-close. Two cuts have cost credibility, so the next catalysts are binary: Q4 delivery against the implied step-up, the evoke closing (Gibraltar court, remaining licences) and the first quantified synergy/pro forma leverage disclosure in Q1-27.
**Share reaction muted:** −1.9% on 20 Nov per Investing.com's slide write-up (level printed as "$1.065", almost certainly €1.065 on Euronext Athens — unverified against the exchange).

segments.name: Bally's International Interactive (BII) — UK & Spain online B2C
segments.headline: UK NGR at a third straight record on +12.2% cc with less marketing, but the 40% duty is still only ~55% offset and the FY26 BII range was cut again to €270–280m; implied Q4 needs a 19–34% sequential jump.
narrative: Bally's International Interactive — the former Gamesys UK bingo/casino-led portfolio consolidated from 8 October 2025 — delivered Q3 revenue of €201.6m (~$221m), up 4.0% (+€7.8m) quarter-on-quarter, taking 9M revenue to €579.2m (~$635m), 70% of the group and +10.9% year-on-year in constant currency on a pro forma basis. The UK, which at €540.6m (~$593m) of 9M revenue is roughly 93% of the division (regional split OCR'd from the release chart), grew online revenue 12.2% cc in Q3 — the third consecutive acceleration (Q1 +10.5%, Q2 +11.6%) and a third straight all-time-high NGR quarter — and did so with marketing lower both year-on-year and sequentially. Spain set a record at €13.3m (~$14.6m), +18.9% YoY and roughly +7% against the ~€12.4m we derive for Q2, on what management describes only as "a larger active player base". No actives, ARPU, product-level (casino vs bingo vs sports) or market-share data are disclosed, so the quality of UK growth — new-player acquisition versus existing-cohort spend — cannot be independently assessed; the falling marketing intensity suggests it is retention- and cross-sell-led, which is encouraging for durability but equally consistent with a business being harvested ahead of a merger.

The P&L is dominated by the 1 April 2026 step-up in UK remote gaming duty from 21% to 40%. The group gaming-tax line was €76.8m (~$84m) in Q3, 26.8% of group revenue and roughly 38% of BII revenue (legacy gaming tax is negligible), versus roughly 22% of BII revenue in pre-duty Q1 (derived). Management puts the gross AEBITDA hit at ~€34m (~$37m) per quarter, ~€68m (~$75m) for 9M. BII AEBITDA was €62.8m (~$69m) in Q3, +4.5% QoQ, at a 31.1% margin (Q2 31.0%, Q1 39.5%); 9M AEBITDA was €195.6m (~$215m) at 33.8%, which we compute as −15.2% against the €230.7m pro forma 9M25 base implied by the company's own bridge (9M25 PF group €320.8m less legacy €90.1m). Ex-duty, management says BII AEBITDA would have grown 14.4%. The bridge attributes +€26.2m to organic gross-profit growth and +€6.8m to fixed-cost actions, i.e. 48.5% of the 9M hit offset; in Q3 the offset was ~55% measured year-on-year, which arithmetically implies only ~42% in Q2 on the same basis. Note the basis change: at H1 management said ~65% of the Q2 hit had been mitigated, measured against the pre-duty run-rate; the Q3 "55%" is on the YoY basis management now says it will use "now that the duty is in every quarter". Reeves called Q2 "the low point"; the Q3 data support that at the margin level, but not yet at a rate that protects the full year.

On costs, group marketing and advertising was €21.7m (~$24m) in Q3, 7.6% of group revenue, versus ~€24.5m per quarter on average in 1H (9M €70.7m, 8.5%); stripping out the legacy run-rate (~€2.6m in 3Q25), BII marketing was roughly €19m, or ~9.5% of divisional revenue, down low-double-digits sequentially on our derivation. The CEO was explicit that he is prioritising revenue growth over further marketing cuts and that the division "hasn't removed as much cost as I may have wanted" because he wants the team ready to "hit the ground running" at evoke completion — BII is therefore carrying integration-readiness cost that depresses the standalone margin. That is the first component of the guidance cut: FY26 BII AEBITDA is now €270–280m (~$296–307m), from €280–295m in August (the top end having been the "consolidation" scenario) and c.€299m at the March plan; Reeves quantified the gap at ~€15m and attributed it to slower UK consolidation — "I expected subscale operators to fall away much faster and their players to move to larger-scale brands" — plus the retained cost base.

The implied Q4 is the issue. BII needs €74.4–84.4m (~$82–93m) of Q4 AEBITDA to land inside the new range, against €62.8m in Q3 — a 19–34% sequential step-up. Q4 is seasonally the strongest UK online quarter and marketing has already been pared, but on our derivation BII's pro forma Q4-25 AEBITDA was only around €70–78m, so the range implies BII more than fully offsets the ~€34m YoY duty hit in Q4 after offsetting 55% in Q3. We regard the bottom of the range as the realistic target and see risk below it. Strategically, management's answer to the duty is scale: the all-share acquisition of evoke (equity value c.£243m / ~€284m / ~$312m per iGB; EV c.€1.6bn per Edison at the indicated 50p) has cleared UK gaming-regulatory and UK merger-control conditions and both shareholder votes (evoke 99.63%), and awaits remaining gaming approvals and the Gibraltar court sanction by end-2026 for a January 2027 close — firmed up from "Q1-27" in the 10 November preliminary release. Until then the two are run as competitors, and no synergy figure has been given beyond "significant cost synergies". The second leg of the November 2025 UK Budget — the remote betting duty increase slated for April 2027 — matters less for a casino/bingo-led book than for evoke's William Hill sportsbook, but it lands in the first full year of combined ownership.

segments.name: Intralot legacy B2B — lottery technology, VLT monitoring & services
segments.headline: US lottery −11% cc on jackpot comps and lower equipment sales; legacy B2B AEBITDA −15.6% cc with the Q3 margin dropping to 32% — the quarter's under-discussed negative, partly offset by a year of contract renewals that buy duration.
narrative: The legacy Intralot B2B segment — lottery systems, VLT monitoring and services across the US, Australia, Europe and Latin America — is 23% of group revenue and remains in mild decline. 9M revenue was €191.0m (~$210m), −8.1% reported and −6.2% in constant currency (group B2B, which includes a small BII B2B contribution, was €191.7m vs €207.8m, −7.7%). The US, the largest market, fell 11.0% cc to €119.6m (~$131m) against a 2025 base inflated by record multi-state jackpots and higher equipment sales; the rest of the portfolio grew 3.6% cc. In Q3, group B2B revenue was €63.1m (~$69m), −3.0% (−€2.0m) QoQ and −3.4% YoY versus €65.3m, with the US "broadly stable" sequentially. By product, lottery is now 20.3% of group revenue (≈€168.6m / ~$185m, derived from the disclosed mix) and VLT monitoring 4.0% (≈€33.2m); regionally, America was ~€150.7m (~$165m) of 9M revenue, −9% on €165.6m (chart-derived, and including Argentina's B2C).

Profitability deteriorated faster than revenue. Legacy B2B AEBITDA was €58.4m (~$64m) for 9M, −17.5% reported / −15.6% cc, with the margin down 350bps to 30.6% from 34.1%. The quarterly pattern is worse than the release lets on: group B2B AEBITDA fell to €20.2m (~$22m) in Q3 from €24.5m in Q2 (−17.6%) and €24.2m in 3Q25 (−16.5%), taking the margin to 32.0% from 37.6% and 37.1% respectively; stripping 1H's €41.2m from the 9M legacy figure implies legacy-only Q3 B2B AEBITDA of roughly €17.2m (~$19m). The release discusses the Q3 B2B movement only as "revenue eased 3.0%"; the €4.3m sequential EBITDA decline is not explained. On the call, asked whether some contracts are effectively mispriced with costs inflating faster than revenue, the B2B leadership conceded "some truth" to the point while stressing cyclicality (fuel prices, point-of-sale visits, jackpots) and the non-recurrence of last year's equipment sales. The normalised-items list is instructive on the cost of defending the franchise: Maryland litigation legal fees and RFP preparation, the recently completed Texas RFP (outcome not disclosed in the release), New York and South Carolina RFP preparation, a Croatia software-delay penalty, an ODIE receivable impairment and a success fee on the Australian renewal.

What 2026 has bought is contract duration. The 15-year Victoria EGM monitoring licence (April; €85.0m / ~$93m premium paid, excluded from the company's FCF definition), OLG Ontario's selection of Intralot Canada as lottery technology provider (June), the PLI Ireland extension to 2034 (July), the Hellenic Lotteries renewal (May), Polla Chilena (April) and BCLC shared services (April) all landed, and in the US the new contracts are live in Montana and Idaho with Arkansas and New Hampshire due in 1H-27; management says this removes the 2026/27 expiry overhang that previously hung over the segment. The cost is in capex — 9M net capex of €133.3m includes US renewal investment on top of the Australian premium — and, we suspect, in renewal economics. Legacy guidance (B2B plus B2C) is now €110–115m (~$121–126m) from €112–120m, with the €5–7.5m gap "depending on jackpots"; the implied Q4 of €31.9–36.9m versus €26.0m in Q3 relies on normal Q4 lottery seasonality and a jackpot run.

Our read is that the lottery annuity remains intact but its margin is being squeezed from both ends — cyclical US sales weakness on a cost base that is sticky, and RFP/renewal spending that is recurring in all but accounting label. Operating-cash conversion remains good (group 9M OCF €206.6m) and the business is the collateral underwriting the €130m retail bond and the €200m Greek bank facility, but it is no longer the earnings-growth engine; we would model legacy B2B AEBITDA broadly flat-to-down into 2027 until the new US contracts ramp and jackpots normalise (estimate).

Normalised items include Maryland litigation and RFP costs, Texas, New York and South Carolina RFPs, Croatia penalty, ODIE impairment and Australian renewal success fee.

Cash conversion good (group 9M OCF €206.6m); business collateralises the €130m retail bond and €200m Greek bank facility but is no longer the growth engine.

segments.name: Intralot legacy B2C — Bilyoner (Turkey) & Argentina
segments.headline: Bilyoner gaining share (wagers +28.4% LC vs market +17.8%) and rebounding 26% QoQ in Q3, but an 18% lira depreciation and a remuneration-structure amendment leave euro revenue up only 3.4%.
narrative: Legacy B2C — Bilyoner in Turkey (online sports betting) and Intralot's Argentine operations — grew 9M revenue 7.1% to €60.1m (~$66m) and was the swing factor in the legacy Q3 recovery. After a weak Q2 in which Bilyoner's revenue fell 21.8% (−€3.6m) QoQ on market seasonality and an amendment to its remuneration structure, Q3 Turkey revenue rebounded 25.8% (+€3.3m) to roughly €16.3m (derived), and Argentina added €0.9m to about €5.4m; on our derivation legacy B2C revenue was ~€21.6m (~$24m) in Q3, up ~23% QoQ and +31% against the €16.5m of legacy-only B2C in 3Q25. Bilyoner is a genuine share-gainer: amounts wagered rose 28.4% in lira versus 17.8% for the Turkish online sports-betting market, and revenue grew 20.6% in local currency — but an 18.2% average lira depreciation against the euro left reported revenue up only 3.4% at €45.8m (~$50m). Argentina grew 21.1% to €14.3m (~$15.7m).

AEBITDA for the sub-segment was €19.7m (~$21.6m) for 9M, +1.8%, with Bilyoner at €16.4m (~$18m; +21.5% LC, +0.6% EUR) and Argentina at €3.3m (~$3.6m; +8.5%); the 9M margin was 32.8%. The Q3 swing was large: group B2C AEBITDA rose €8.6m QoQ, of which Bilyoner alone contributed €4.7m (CFO), reversing the €3.2m decline it had inflicted between Q1 and Q2; stripping 1H's €10.9m from the 9M figure gives legacy B2C Q3 AEBITDA of about €8.8m (~$9.7m), a ~41% margin, versus €5.7m in 3Q25. A fine following a KYC compliance review in Turkey sits in the normalised items, as does the 1H remuneration change that is not quantified.

At ~7% of group revenue and ~7% of AEBITDA this is not thesis-moving, but it matters for guidance credibility: the "led by Bilyoner and Argentina" legacy Q3 recovery is a lira- and seasonality-driven B2C story masking a B2B margin decline, and the Q4 legacy implied step-up assumes Bilyoner holds its Q3 level into Turkey's seasonally strong winter football calendar. The remuneration-structure amendment is a permanent take-rate haircut, and the lira remains the dominant translation risk; management's new guidance now explicitly embeds TRY. No handle in euro terms, net margin, actives or ARPU are disclosed for Bilyoner, so we cannot separate volume from hold.

Argentina is small but clean — +21.1% revenue and +8.5% AEBITDA for 9M, with a lower incremental margin that suggests either mix or peso effects; it adds little to the group equity story beyond diversification of the legacy B2C line.

highlights.text: UK online revenue +12.2% cc YoY in Q3 — a third consecutive acceleration (10.5% → 11.6% → 12.2%) and third straight record NGR quarter, achieved with marketing down YoY and QoQ (group marketing €21.7m, 7.6% of revenue, vs ~€24.5m/qtr in 1H). Evidence that scale brands can grow through a 40% duty.
Spain online at a record €13.3m (~$14.6m), +18.9% YoY on a larger active base — small (~6–7% of BII) but a second growth leg outside the UK.

Sequential recovery: Q3 AEBITDA €88.9m (~$97.5m), +5.1% QoQ, margin +50bps to 31.1%; BII AEBITDA +€2.7m QoQ to €62.8m; duty offset improved to ~55% YoY from ~42% implied for Q2; management says Q2 was the low point.

Bilyoner is taking share — wagers +28.4% LC vs a Turkish market +17.8%, revenue +20.6% LC, AEBITDA +21.5% LC — and drove a €4.7m QoQ AEBITDA swing in Q3; Argentina +21.1% revenue. Translation (TRY −18.2%) hides it in euros.

Liquidity rebuilt to €472.4m (~$518m) from €287.3m: £261.8m (~€306m / ~$336m) three-year senior secured sterling term facility signed in July, Tranche A £157.1m drawn, €65m RCF repaid, €160m RCF fully undrawn; adjusted net debt flat QoQ at €1,629.9m (~$1.79bn).

evoke de-risked: UK gaming-regulatory and UK merger-control conditions satisfied, evoke shareholders 99.63% in favour, BYLOT EGM done; close firmed to January 2027 from "Q1-27" ten days earlier. The scale answer to the duty is arriving.

Lottery contract duration restored: Victoria 15-year EGM monitoring, OLG Ontario, PLI Ireland to 2034, Hellenic Lotteries, Polla Chilena, BCLC; US go-lives in Montana and Idaho with Arkansas/New Hampshire in 1H-27 — the 2026/27 expiry overhang is gone.

lowlights.text: Second FY26 AEBITDA cut in three months: €380–395m (~$417–433m) vs €402–415m in August and ~€422m in March/May; midpoint −8% from the original plan. ~€15m of the gap is BII (slower UK consolidation, cost deliberately retained for evoke), €5–7.5m legacy (jackpots). Credibility is now the scarce resource.

Implied Q4 looks stretched: guidance needs Q4 AEBITDA of €106–121m vs €88.9m in Q3 and ~€103m pro forma in Q4-25 (derived) — flat-to-up YoY despite ~€34m of incremental duty. BII alone needs €74–84m vs €62.8m (+19–34% QoQ), i.e. >100% duty offset after 55% in Q3.

The duty is only half-mitigated: 48.5% of the ~€68m (~$75m) 9M gross hit offset; BII AEBITDA −15% YoY pro forma to €195.6m with the margin at 33.8% vs 39.5% in pre-duty Q1; group gaming tax €192.2m (23% of revenue). Ex-duty growth of +14.4% is real but not bankable.

Legacy B2B profitability is falling faster than revenue: 9M AEBITDA €58.4m (~$64m), −15.6% cc, margin 30.6% vs 34.1%; group B2B AEBITDA −€4.3m QoQ in Q3 to €20.2m (32.0% margin vs 37.6%) on only −€2.0m of revenue — unexplained in the release, and management conceded "some truth" to the mispriced-contracts question.

Leverage up to 4.33x PF from 4.05x as the duty annualises; NIATMI −€40.9m (~−$45m); net finance cost €109.7m (~$120m); FCFE €54.5m (~$60m) versus €55.5m of dividends, buybacks and TRS collateral — shareholder returns funded by new sterling debt ahead of a leveraging acquisition, with a €43.3m TRS liability outside the debt definition.

The duty-mitigation KPI changed basis: ~65% at H1 (vs pre-duty run-rate) became ~55% at Q3 on a YoY basis, which implies Q2 was ~42% on the new basis. The direction is improving, but the optics have been managed.

One-off noise accumulating: €27.7m (~$30m) transaction fees in 9M, Turkish KYC fine, Croatia software-delay penalty, ODIE receivable impairment, Maryland litigation and multi-state RFP costs (Texas outcome undisclosed), €85.0m Australian licence premium excluded from the FCF definition; TRY −18.2% and GBP translation (€7.5m adverse FX on sterling loans).

forecast.intro: The FY26 guidance bridge is a two-step walk-down driven roughly 70/30 by BII and legacy. The March plan (~€422m, reaffirmed with Q1) assumed c.€299m from International Interactive and c.€124m from legacy Intralot. In August, after the first full quarter at 40% RGD, BII was cut to €280–295m (the top end conditional on UK consolidation) and legacy to €112–120m. On 20 November BII went to €270–280m and legacy to €110–115m — €380–395m (~$417–433m) combined. The moving parts, per the CEO: UK consolidation slower than assumed (sub-scale operators not exiting post-duty), cost base deliberately retained for evoke integration, a weak US jackpot environment, and GBP/USD/TRY translation now explicitly inside the range. What has not moved is the UK top line, which keeps accelerating.

forecast.view: **Revenue:** we model FY26 group revenue of ~€1.12–1.13bn (~$1.23–1.24bn): 9M €830.3m plus a Q4 of ~€290–300m, with BII at ~€205–210m on normal UK Q4 seasonality and legacy ~€85–90m on lottery Q4 seasonality and a steady Bilyoner (estimate). **AEBITDA:** we sit at ~€375–385m (~$411–422m), at or just below the bottom of the new range — BII ~€265–272m (Q4 €70–76m, assuming the YoY duty offset improves to ~65% against a derived Q4-25 base of ~€70–78m) and legacy ~€108–112m (Q4 €30–34m). Hitting the midpoint requires BII to offset >100% of the Q4 duty hit; we do not underwrite that after 42%/55% in Q2/Q3. **Margin:** FY26 ~33–34%; Q4 ~35–36% on seasonality and low marketing. **Leverage:** year-end adjusted net debt ~€1.60–1.65bn (Q4 FCF seasonally positive, no further licence payments disclosed, TRS purchases ongoing) gives standalone PF leverage of ~4.2–4.4x; the real number is post-evoke, where evoke's own debt (EV c.€1.6bn per Edison) and ~18% EBITDA margin dilute group margin toward the high-20s before synergies — the first synergy quantification in Q1-27 is the single most important disclosure ahead. **2027 shape (estimate):** UK duty stops being a YoY headwind after Q1-27; UK revenue +8–10% with marketing held; remote betting duty step-up in April 2027 is a modest headwind for BII's casino-led book but a real one for William Hill; legacy flat-ish as Arkansas/New Hampshire go live and jackpots mean-revert. Swing factors: Q4 UK NGR and marketing, US jackpot runs, TRY, the Gibraltar court timetable and any CMA/licence surprise, and refinancing of the €130m 6.00% retail bond due 2029 within a 4x+ structure.
watch: Q4-26 BII AEBITDA ≥ €74m (bottom of guidance) and the YoY duty-offset ratio moving from ~55% toward ≥65% — the acid test of both the consolidation thesis and guidance credibility; also whether management keeps the YoY measurement basis.

evoke closing mechanics: remaining gaming approvals and Gibraltar court sanction by end-December, January 2027 completion, then the first quantified cost-synergy target and pro forma combined leverage (we expect well above 4x at close).

US lottery: jackpot cycle through the holiday season, Arkansas and New Hampshire go-lives in 1H-27, the Maryland RFP outcome and litigation, and the undisclosed Texas RFP result; any sign of renewal-driven margin dilution in legacy B2B.

UK regulatory second leg: the April 2027 remote betting duty increase (Nov-25 Budget) and any further affordability/stake-limit moves; evidence (or not) of sub-scale operator exits that management's thesis depends on.
FX translation: TRY (−18.2% avg in 9M) on Bilyoner, GBP on both BII earnings and the £557m of sterling term debt (€7.5m adverse non-cash FX in 9M), USD on US lottery.

Capital allocation and governance: TRS share purchases via Deutsche Bank and dividends while PF leverage is 4.33x and rising; Fitch Negative outlook (per secondary sources); the €130m retail bond 2029 and RCF covenant headroom; Bally's Corp control and related-party flows.

Disclosure gaps that would change the analysis: actives/ARPU/product split for BII, legacy B2B quarterly EBITDA (the Q3 −€4.3m QoQ drop was unexplained), and detail on Bilyoner's amended remuneration structure.
